insights.claim: The net trade float is RON -2,633,068.76: RON 27,193.95 owed by customers against RON 2,660,262.71 owed to suppliers — 61.1 days of sales outstanding against not reported of payables, a gap of not reported.
insights.claim_template: The net trade float is {money:float}: {money:trade_receivables} owed by customers against {money:trade_payables} owed to suppliers — {measure:dso} of sales outstanding against {measure:dpo} of payables, a gap of {measure:float_days}.
insights.formula: DSO = trade receivables net ÷ revenue × 365; DPO = trade payables ÷ cost of goods sold × 365; float = trade receivables net − trade payables

narrative.explanation: The net trade float is RON -2,633,068.76: RON 27,193.95 owed by customers against RON 2,660,262.71 owed to suppliers — 61.1 days of sales outstanding against not reported of payables, a gap of not reported. Graded critical: the amount at stake is 1,621.7% of revenue, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Compare the collection gap with the credit terms actually granted. Where suppliers fund the cycle, that funding is a payables line that can be withdrawn, not a permanent source.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.

insights.claim_template: Rebuilding the P&L from the movement columns reaches {money:reconstructed}; statutory profit in account 121 is {money:statutory}. The unexplained step of {money:step} is {measure:graded_share} of the {money:graded_base} it is bridging.

measures.label: Net income rebuilt from the movements
Step as a share of reconstructed net income

narrative.explanation: Rebuilding the P&L from the movement columns reaches RON -30,391,418.38; statutory profit in account 121 is RON -801,604.14. Graded critical: the amount at stake is 97.4% of reconstructed net income, against the ladder printed beside this finding. The step is graded against the profit it is correcting. A bridge worth a tenth of the answer is a footnote; one worth half of it means the reconstruction is not the source of the printed profit.

narrative.so_what: Ask for the year-end journals behind the step to account 121 before relying on the reconstructed P&L for anything. A large bridge means the movement columns are not the source of the reported profit.

insights.claim: The current ratio of 2.72× falls to 2.46× once RON 7,492,271.51 of non-trade receivables is removed; the cash ratio is 0.04×.
insights.claim_template: The current ratio of {measure:current_ratio} falls to {measure:current_ratio_trade_only} once {money:non_trade} of non-trade receivables is removed; the cash ratio is {measure:cash_ratio}.
insights.formula: Current ratio recomputed with non-trade receivables (intercompany, other debtors, supplier advances, tax recoverable) removed from current assets

narrative.explanation: The current ratio of 2.72× falls to 2.46× once RON 7,492,271.51 of non-trade receivables is removed; the cash ratio is 0.04×. Graded medium: the amount at stake is 26.6% of total current liabilities, against the ladder printed beside this finding. The excluded assets are graded against the liabilities they were being counted as cover for, which is the same denominator the current ratio itself uses — so the severity IS the ratio movement.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Read the current ratio in its trade-only form when setting covenant headroom. The non-trade balances removed here are not stock that converts on ordinary terms, and a lender will discount them.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

insights.claim: RON 16,620.28 of operating income is other operating income and provision reversals rather than trading margin — 10.2% of RON 162,365.46; the operating cash proxy is RON -739,384.70 against an EBITDA of RON -29,038,838.12, a conversion of 2.5%.
insights.claim_template: {money:non_trading} of operating income is other operating income and provision reversals rather than trading margin — {measure:graded_share} of {money:graded_base}; the operating cash proxy is {money:cash_proxy} against an EBITDA of {money:ebitda}, a conversion of {measure:cash_conversion}.
insights.formula: (Other operating income + provision reversals) ÷ EBITDA; operating cash proxy ÷ EBITDA; capitalised own work

measures.label: Other operating income and provision reversals
Non-trading income as a share of revenue

narrative.explanation: RON 16,620.28 of operating income is other operating income and provision reversals rather than trading margin — 10.2% of RON 162,365.46; the operating cash proxy is RON -739,384.70 against an EBITDA of RON -29,038,838.12, a conversion of 2.5%. Graded medium: the amount at stake is 10.2% of revenue, against the ladder printed beside this finding. ebitda is not a usable scale on this book, so the finding is graded against revenue instead. Non-trading income is graded against the EBITDA it is inside, so the severity answers "how much of this margin is not trading" rather than "is this a big number".
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Strip the non-trading income out before applying any multiple. Provision reversals and other operating income do not recur, and an EBITDA that leans on them overstates the run rate.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: ebitda is not a usable scale on this book, so the finding is graded against revenue instead. Non-trading income is graded against the EBITDA it is inside, so the severity answers "how much of this margin is not trading" rather than "is this a big number".

insights.claim: 48.3% of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of RON 6,616,104.38 carries 106.3 years of life at the current annual charge of RON 62,219.44.
insights.claim_template: {measure:depreciated_share} of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of {money:net_book_value} carries {measure:remaining_book_life} of life at the current annual charge of {money:annual_da}.
insights.formula: Accumulated depreciation ÷ gross PP&E; net book value ÷ annual D&A = remaining book life

measures.label: Remaining book life at current charge

narrative.explanation: 48.3% of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of RON 6,616,104.38 carries 106.3 years of life at the current annual charge of RON 62,219.44. Graded low: the amount at stake is 48.3% of gross pp&e, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Ask for the fixed-asset register by acquisition year and the committed capex plan. A book this far through its depreciation life either has replacement spending ahead of it or is running assets past their useful life, and the two have very different cash consequences.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.
